messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: delayed ingestion detected in Datadog (eu-west-1 + partial us). Gaps in logs/metrics/traces. Auto-escalating to #incidents. https://status.datadoghq.com/incident/xxxxx

emma (sre-oncall): paging @oncall-eng-sre @infra-oncall — seeing a ~5m hole in host metrics + traces. Dashboards showing stale data; marking P1 until we understand scope. Anyone on-call?

raj (infra-oncall): I'm online. Confirming gaps. Cloud provider metrics (CloudWatch) look normal, no signs of app-side backpressure. Datadog UI shows "Ingestion delayed / rate limiting". Opening a support incident: INC-123789.

maria (eng-runtime): Checked dd-agent logs on forwarders: connections ESTABLISHED; HTTP 200s on batch posts but huge latency on the transport layer. No auth failures. Likely upstream queuing at Datadog.

emma (sre-oncall): Ok. Short mitigation plan (execute in parallel):
- flip critical ops panels to CloudWatch/Prometheus queries
- enable forwarder S3 fallback for raw logs
- increase on-disk buffer for local agents
- enable local trace dump for key services (payments/webhooks)
- notify impacted customers (SLA-sensitive)

dan (product-support): I'll prepare a customer advisory. Current message: "We're investigating an observability degradation caused by a third-party ingestion incident (Datadog). Application functionality not reported as impacted; some traces and logs may be delayed. We'll update every 30 minutes." Targeting enterprise contacts first.

raj (infra-oncall): Swapping dashboards: attaching Prometheus node/exporter queries into the ops panel now. Also suppressing alerts that depend on Datadog-derived rollups to avoid noise.

maria (eng-runtime): Command to enable s3 fallback on forwarders (run on forwarder fleet):

```
# enable temporary S3 sink and increase buffer
dd-logs-forwarder configure --buffer 600MB --s3-bucket redwood-incident-dumps --s3-prefix incident-1769580000/ --flush-interval 10m
systemctl restart dd-logs-forwarder
```

maria (eng-runtime): Rolling this out to hosts in batches. Watching local queues.

datadog-status-bot: Datadog: "Investigating an issue impacting ingestion in several regions; delays for logs/metrics/traces." (latest update)

emma (sre-oncall): Also enable trace capture for payments at 100% sampling to disk so we can replay traces if Datadog processing never arrives. Ensure dumps are encrypted and uploaded to S3.

maria (eng-runtime): Trace capture enabled for service=payments -> /var/local/trace-captures/incident-1769580000/ (encrypted). Will start s3 archival when files hit 200MB.

dan (product-support): Sent initial advisory to top-10 SLA customers. Responses so far: noted, no immediate impact reported. I'll keep the cadence and escalate if any customer reports data loss.

emma (sre-oncall): Action owners: raj -> dashboard fallback + alert mapping; maria -> s3 fallback + trace dumps; dan -> customer comms; emma -> coordinate with Datadog support + timeline.

raj (infra-oncall): Dashboard fallback complete. Verified CloudWatch/Prometheus metrics align with host telemetry. Suppressed 7 noisy alerts that were firing due to missing Datadog aggregates.

maria (eng-runtime): Forwarders started S3 upload, initial batches archived. We saw a brief spike in local disk usage; increased rotation and eviction to keep <75% disk. Trace dump files being written.

datadog-status-bot: Update from Datadog: "Backlog processing in progress; partial ingestion restoration seen for some customers."

emma (sre-oncall): Good. I'll stay on until handoff. Handoff note in 40m: @devon will take over. Key watch items for next shift:
- Datadog support updates (INC-123789) and status page updates
- Confirm backlog shows historical metrics/traces (reconcile against CloudWatch/Prometheus)
- Ensure all local archives uploaded and accessible to support teams
- Keep customer comms every 30m or on material changes

devon (sre-next): Ack, will join in ~10m and take over handoff. Please post the runbook.

emma (sre-oncall): Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/observability-datadog-ingest-fallback (contains checklist and postmortem template)

dan (product-support): Next customer update scheduled in 30m. Also triaging inbound tickets to translate missing telemetry into potential user-impact items.

maria (eng-runtime): Note: a small number of forwarders hit temporary I/O pressure; we rotated old dumps to S3 faster which stabilized disks. KMS keys verified for encrypting archives.

datadog-status-bot: New message: "Processing backlog; many customers seeing data return within the hour. Traces may remain delayed longer."

devon (sre-next): Took over — current state: some backlog visible, traces slowly reappearing for a subset of hosts. Maintaining P1 until we can reconcile full coverage. Capturing timeline for postmortem.

emma (sre-oncall): Leaving handoff. Postmortem TODOs: timeline of alert triggers, dashboards affected, mitigation actions and costs (S3 egress/ingestion), list of customers notified, suggestion to evaluate multi-provider alerting for critical SLOs.

devon (sre-next): I'll own the postmortem draft and follow up on action items. Adding suggestion: automated fallback alerts to CloudWatch for defined critical metrics.

dan (product-support): Customers marked as "monitoring" for now until full ingestion confirmed. No escalations at this time.

maria (eng-runtime): Final note before wrap: all uploaded archives are accessible and checksummed. Updating INC-123789 with s3 URLs for Datadog support if they need to replay data.

datadog-status-bot: FINAL UPDATE (thread snapshot): Datadog reports recovery in affected regions; backlog processing ongoing. Recommend validating data completeness before closing the incident.

participants: emma (sre-oncall), raj (infra-oncall), maria (eng-runtime), dan (product-support), devon (sre-next), incident-bot, datadog-status-bot

post-incident followups: INC-123789 assigned; postmortem owner: devon; next steps include runbook revisions, multi-provider alert experiment, and cost review for temporary S3 archival."
